reviewer: root after full-design binding and independent source/logic comparison
reason: The actual design is restricted to multi-item lists under a shared predicate; examples of clause coordination do not refute that restricted mechanism. Its selected unit already requires a shared predicate, while its comparator lacks shared-predicate structure, risking outcome-conditioned selection. An item noun can occur in such lists, so a no-scope-association prediction does not follow from the noun rival. Boundary sensitivity blocks the proposed measurement, not coordination in general.

all_of.detail: Freeze an independently justified parse or explicit alternative parses and the candidate inventory before selecting by list outcome. Declare how the list-coordinator and item-noun models differ after allowing noun participation in lists. Use held data with a discriminating candidate-position/scope prediction and adequate power. Resolve source-group uncertainty or preserve it without treating one convenient segmentation as semantic gold.

Bind the chosen semantic and source-boundary annotations independently of candidate identity and inherited renderer labels. Apply the relevant relation gates if an ordered inscription packet is proposed.

not_sufficient: A structural association compatible with both declared models.
Out-of-scope ordinary-language examples treated as empirical rejection of the restricted mechanism.
More pages without the missing discriminator or annotation binding.
